6986-hygienic-physiology-with-special-re:
Joel Dorman Steele's Hygienic Physiology, third in the Pathfinder series, teaches advanced pupils the human body with special reference to alcoholic drinks and narcotics. It revises his Fourteen Weeks in Human Physiology in an enlarged edition with selected readings, edited for schools under recent temperance instruction laws. The series runs from a child's health primer through hygiene for young people to this volume.

An 1889 endorsement notes the books were written by experts under the Scientific Department of the National Woman's Christian Temperance Union, and revised to keep pace with science. The aim is plain teaching on health, habit, and the effects of drink and drugs. Steele writes for classrooms where temperance law required such lessons.
doe-osti-3403174-autosac-automated-sampl:
Report ORNL/TM-2026/4694 from Oak Ridge National Laboratory, by Ke An, dated July 2026, describes AutoSAC, a tool that works out sample activation on the VULCAN instrument. VULCAN is a neutron beam instrument, and users need to know how active a sample becomes. The tool runs inside the normal data pipeline.

AutoSAC takes a CINDER library file and uses an open source isotope library at present. Beam flux is measured by an imaging camera at the sample spot, under set guide layouts. The tool can join the auto reduction pipeline once a measurement ends. Beam users get a faster, more standard check of sample activity.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIFOIARecordsG:
A letter from the U.S. Department of Justice went to Congressman Louis Stokes about the House Select Committee on Assassinations report. Stokes had chaired the committee, which reopened the Kennedy and King cases in the late 1970s. The department wrote to tell him the results of its own review of the committee's report.

Such letters close the loop between an inquiry and the department it examines. The committee had judged the Justice Department's earlier work, and now the department answered on paper. The letter preserves that official response, part of the long paper argument over how the assassinations were investigated.
hygienic-physiology-with-special-referen:
Joel Dorman Steele's Hygienic Physiology teaches the science of the human body, with attention to drink and drugs. The book is a new, longer version of his Fourteen Weeks in Human Physiology, made for schools under the drink-teaching laws then spreading across America.

Steele's Pathfinder series served young, middle and older pupils, and this third book was aimed at the oldest group. Skilled writers made the series for the science office of the Woman's Christian Temperance Union, and chosen readings back up the lessons. Readers keen on Victorian health teaching, or on how the drink reform cause entered the classroom, will find Steele clear, earnest and true to his time.
